newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bank Labouchere says '97 net may match '96.
newsitem.headline: Bank Labouchere says '97 net may match '96.

text.p: Bank Labouchere, a fully-owned banking unit of Dutch insurer Aegon said on Wednesday that 1997 had started well and if favourable market trends persisted full-year profits could match those of 1996.
"In the event of favourable market developments in 1997, the highly favourable (net) profit level of 1996 can be equalled," Labouchere said in a statement.

The bank earlier reported 1996 profits almost doubled to 37.68 million guilders from a year-earlier 19.05 million, helped in part by a 5.32 million one-off net gain resulting from the sale of money market broker Wallich & Matthes.
Labouchere chairman Jos Streppel said that should the stock market fail to rise this year as much as it had in 1996, Labouchere would still achieve a good level of profits.

"We have become a good deal less vulnerable to bourse trends," he said, adding Labouchere had increased the proportion of its income derived from "embedded value" services, such as private banking, resulting in a more structurally constant stream of income.
Asked what constituted a good level of profits, Streppel said "a less than 12 percent (net) return on equity would bring tears to my eyes," adding that 1997 had started well.
